name: Young Circle baobab (south end)

location.address: ArtsPark at Young Circle, 1 Young Circle, Hollywood, FL 33020

official_register.name: Florida Forest Service Champion Tree Register

access: Free. ArtsPark at Young Circle is a city park open 7:00 AM to 11:00 PM daily (City of Hollywood page); ADA accessible, street parking.
verify_notes: Register: Florida Champion (Broward), circumference 416 in = 1057 cm, height 55 ft = 16.8 m, crown 78x74 ft, measured 2016-02-22 (register date field 1456099200000). Register location text: south end of the park. City of Hollywood page says the park is 'one of the few places in the United States where you can see five Baobab Trees' and calls baobabs 'the second widest species of tree in the world'. Planting date and planter undocumented: nursery page says locally believed 1930s-1940s; monumentaltrees.com (cross-check only) reasons ~1926 from a 1935 photo of the circle (then Harding Circle); a Substack blog argues far older from African growth rates, a blog inference, not used. Do not state an age. Dispute noted, no source names a planter, nothing links J. W. Young. A fountain in the park (Millennium Springs, Ritsuko Taho) is tied to the energy waves of one baobab (search snippet, not fetched; leave out unless seen). Pin = register coordinate in the park, not shown to land on one crown, so approximate. Sits ~115 m from ftl_006 (the park's other registered baobab); both could be told as one stop at Young Circle. Alive: city page current, register measured 2016, lifecheck NONE; 'flagged' thin alive evidence, no dated recent photo seen. One source plus city page (US bar met).
